title: data simulation
description:
Real data with some supplemented prototype points to increase nonlinearity.

Takes a set of known prototype points, samples from them, and generates correlated bivariate normal predictors. 

The `difficulty` arg can be used to modulate how easy the problem is. 

Seed is an argument defaulted to 2026.  

``` r
library(tidymodels)
#> Warning: package 'dials' was built under R version 4.6.1
theme_set(theme_bw())

source("~/talks/workshops/slides/sim_2026_conf_data.R")

sim_2026_conf_data(2000, difficulty = 1) |> 
  ggplot(aes(pred_1, pred_2, col = class)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 2/4) + 
  coord_obs_pred() + 
  labs(title = "Difficulty: 1.0")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/IPJHqyX.png)<!-- -->

``` r

sim_2026_conf_data(2000) |> 
  ggplot(aes(pred_1, pred_2, col = class)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 2/4) + 
  coord_obs_pred() + 
  labs(title = "Difficulty: 1.5")
```

description:
## Summary
Fix critical severity security issue in `_freeze/site_libs/leaflet-providers-2.0.0/leaflet-providers_2.0.0.js`.

## Vulnerability
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **ID** | V-001 |
| **Severity** | CRITICAL |
| **Scanner** | multi_agent_ai |
| **Rule** | `V-001` |
| **File** | `_freeze/site_libs/leaflet-providers-2.0.0/leaflet-providers_2.0.0.js:127` |
| **Assessment** | Likely exploitable |

**Description**: The leaflet-providers library contains placeholder API keys in client-side JavaScript code. While these are marked as placeholders, the code structure demonstrates that API keys are intended to be embedded in client-side code. If developers follow this pattern with real API keys, they would be exposed to all users who download the JavaScript file.

## Evidence

**Exploitation scenario**: An attacker can inspect the publicly accessible JavaScript file by viewing page source or downloading the file directly.

**Scanner confirmation**: multi_agent_ai rule `V-001` flagged this pattern.

**Production code**: This file is in the production codebase, not test-only code.

## Changes
- `_freeze/site_libs/leaflet-providers-2.0.0/leaflet-providers_2.0.0.js`

## Behavior Preservation
The change is scoped to 1 file on the vulnerable path, and the project's existing tests still pass, so intended behavior is unchanged.

- [x] Scanner re-scan confirms fix
- [x] LLM code review passed

title: add Claude Code GHA
description:
The Copilot integration worked but much too noisy / too many notifications. Trying out the async Claude Code integration--this PR was otherwise automatically generated by `/install-github-app`.

<details>
  <summary>The default description</summary>

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!
</details>

title: transition to georgia data in introductory workshop
description:
A first pass; just the most basic changes. Will need to make a pass through and make sure that EDA and modeling concepts are still demonstrated as intended.

Prompt:

> This repository contains workshop materials for two tidymodels workshops, intro and advanced.
> 
> I'm working on the introductory workshop. I just made changes to the underlying data from the forested package:
> 
> * The first version of the package just had data from Washington, called `forested`. The second release of the package also includes data from Georgia. The `forested` data is the same as it was, and now is aliased as `forested_wa`. The data from Georgia is called `forested_ga`. The Georgia data has the same structure, except is missing the `northness` variable due to issues with the source raster. `forested_ga` also includes a new variable `county`.
>
>* `forested` and its alias `forested_wa` gained a new variable, `county`.
>
> forested is my own package. I have this developmental version installed; it will be on CRAN by the time participants see it.
> 
> I would like to transition the introductory workshop to use the `forested_ga` data instead of the `forested` data. Could you make that happen? Update the slides starting with `intro-` in `slides/` as well as `classwork/` (if needed). Note that the package, the dataset, and the target variable were called `forested`, so you can't just find and replace on that. Both the package and target variable are still called `forested`.

title: transition from `taxi` to `forested`
description:
A first pass at transitioning from the taxi data to [forested](https://github.com/simonpcouch/forested). 

Tried to mostly stick to finding + replacing for this first PR, dropping `TODO`s where our previous discussion / interpretation needs some reworking. Process was: add `library(forested)` in setup, search for `tip` to make sure there weren't bad substitutions (like "multiple") and then replace with `forested`, replace `taxi` with `forested`.

For the most part, metrics tend to improve in the same situations when they did for the taxi data, so that will save us larger refactorings. That said:

* The outcome classes are much more balanced in this problem, so the `accuracy()` discussion might need some reworking.
* We no longer need to set `cost_complexity` to get a reasonably teachable tree back. I _think_ we intentionally set `cost_complexity` to a lower value when we're not plotting the trees (i.e. after deck 3) to get more solid performance. The previous `cost_complexity = 0.0001` returns a reasonable tree in that case. With that in mind, maybe we should set `cost_complexity` to its default value explicitly so that unexpectedly seeing `cost_complexity` doesn't confuse people.
* The time-based split extra will need a proper rewrite, which I've left for another PR.
* The recipes extra deserves a good bit more attention as well.

We also still have:

``` r
files <- list.files(recursive = TRUE)
files <- files[!grepl("archive|docs", files)]
grep("taxi", files, value = TRUE)
#> [1] "slides/images/taxi_spinning.svg" "slides/images/taxi.png"         
#> [3] "slides/taxi_raw.R"               "slides/taxi_raw.rds"
```

(`taxi_raw` is for the time-based split content.)

Obviously lots more to do, but should be a good place to jump off from / create issues based off of. :) I'm able to `quarto::render()` without issue.

title: Use `parallelly::availableCores()` everywhere
description:
Because `parallel::detectCores()` won't respect your "allocated" amount of cores. In the 2022 tidymodels rstudio conf workshop, our rstudio cloud instances technically had 16 cores available to them, but users were only allocated 2 of them. `parallel::detectCores()` returned `16`, causing `makePSOCKcluster()` to hang indefinitely.

Thanks for parallelly @HenrikBengtsson 😄, this is the first time where this has ever actually been an issue for me. Switching to parallelly fixed it immediately

title: Adjustments to deck 3 (what makes a model)
description: A few recommended changes we can discuss: ### Model introduction The current "All models are wrong" structure is a little stretched, since there are many slides saying "All models are wrong..." with specific details before the payoff of "some are useful". Instead, I made that be a conclusion slide (could also put it at the front of that section) Plotted a decision tree alongside the explanation, since I think it's a useful visual aid for what we mean by a series of if statements ### "Your turn" linear models For the modeling "Your turn", made the exercise about fitting and then extracting from a linear fit. To set that up, I made it more explicit earlier to call the linear model `linear_wflow` in the classwork. ### Other * Moved the "additional ways to understand `tree_fit`" (`vip`, `DALEXtra`, etc) slide a few slides later, after the specifics of tree plotting * Added `glm` to the list of ways to fit a linear model * Added an intro slide for Vetiver, and some notes for a live-code

title: Add notes document to slides
description:
This PR is a proof of concept of slide Notes in a separate document. It is shown here working for 01-introduction

Setup required 2 things:

1. adding  `include-after-body: footer-notes.html` in yaml header.

This adds a small bit of js that modifies the footer of each slide to include a link to the corresponding section of the notes document.

2. Creating the notes document

The annotations document. The document (see slides/annotations.qmd) follows a simple pattern. With titles mimicking the slides and links back to the slides.

# Pro

- Very minimal changes to the slides
- Everything uses relative paths so it can be moved into archived

# Con

- All headers needs to be unique across slides
    - Adding `{#new-id}` to a header changes the id
- Annotations document have to created fairly manual
    - And should thus be created after slides are stable as the notes section have no way to see what is in the slides

title: Initial slide styling
description:
This PR starts styling of the slides.

The styling is done using a custom [reveal themes](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/themes.html) named `tidymodels.scss` modeled after https://github.com/topepo/2022-AZ-keynote. There is not a lot going on in this file, a lot of sass variables are defined.

A `.inverse` class is added as well. and you apply it to a slide by setting the class of the slide to `.inverse`.

Lastly an updated `hexes()` function has been added. Note that this new version uses `...` to pass in the hex names.

I can update the theme as we start to add more different types of elements, so we can merge whenever.

The `hexes()` function is located in a `setup.R` file which is loaded into each .qmd file with the chunk for consistency. This file would be a great place to set default ggplot2 themes, load packages etc etc

````
```{r}
#| include: false
#| file: setup.R
```
````
